problem: "Large β: the snake refuses to bend, so it flattens and can shrink away from a weak edge." The shrinking under a weak edge is caused mainly by α (the length/stretch term acting like a taut rubber band). Large β makes the closed curve stiff and smooth, so it cannot bend into corners, dents or narrow concavities and cuts across them; it does not itself make the snake shrink.
fix: "Large β: the snake refuses to bend, so it stays stiff and smooth; it cannot follow sharp corners or narrow dents and cuts straight across them."

problem: "A large β with a weak edge makes the snake shrink on its own" repeats the same mixing of roles: shrinkage when the edge is weak is an α effect. With large β and a weak edge the curve instead becomes too rigid to enter concave parts of the boundary.
fix: "A large α with a weak edge makes the snake shrink on its own like a taut rubber band; a large β makes it too stiff to bend into corners and dents."

problem: "the second difference vᵢ₊₁ − 2vᵢ + vᵢ₋₁ is large exactly where the curve bends sharply" is only true when the sample points are evenly spaced. Uneven spacing also makes the second difference non-zero on a straight part of the contour.
fix: "the second difference vᵢ₊₁ − 2vᵢ + vᵢ₋₁ is large where the curve bends sharply (for evenly spaced points); uneven spacing between samples also raises it."

problem: "square every side length, do not take square roots at the last step" is confusing, and it contradicts the worked example, which does write √5 = 2.236 and then squares it. A student may read it as "never take a square root" or as "square the side length twice".
fix: "each term |vᵢ₊₁ − vᵢ|² is (Δx)² + (Δy)², so compute it without a square root; write the final answer as a sum of squared lengths, not a sum of side lengths."
